Promise - long column article

The Promise object represents the eventual completion or failure of an asynchronous operation. LONGCOL_BODY_A here marks the main prose.

A Promise is a proxy for a value not necessarily known when the promise is created, letting you associate handlers with the eventual outcome.

Here we create a promise that resolves after a delay, then chain a transformation on the resolved value before logging the final result. LONGCOL_BODY_B.

Promise combinators such as all, allSettled, any, and race let you coordinate multiple concurrent tasks and aggregate their settled outcomes.

Error propagation flows down the chain until a rejection handler is found, which makes fallback strategies straightforward to express in code.

An async function always returns a promise, and await pauses execution until the awaited promise settles, preserving a linear control flow.

Microtask scheduling guarantees that continuation callbacks run after the current synchronous work completes but before any timer callbacks. LONGCOL_BODY_C.
